validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED at high tier by a chain of primary, non-GEM sources of two genuinely different origins. (1) A 208-page Kazakh-government-hosted EIA/working-design document (gov.kz, dated 16.11.2020, downloaded directly and read in full with pdftotext -layout) is literally the environmental-impact filing by AO 'Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya' (Intergas Central Asia, a QazaqGaz subsidiary) titled 'Construction of a reserve gas pipeline (looping) Du1020mm, 130 km long, to the existing Makat-North Caucasus main gas pipeline on the 0-130 km section, Makat and Redut LPU' — an unambiguous, detailed engineering description of exactly this asset (from km 0 CS Makat to km 130 CS Redut, Du1020mm, design throughput 13,146,640,080 m3/year). (2) The Government of Kazakhstan's own 'Integrated Plan for Development of the Gas Industry of the Republic of Kazakhstan for 2022-2026' (Resolution No.488, adilet.zan.kz — a Cabinet-level legal-portal document, a wholly different institutional origin from the Intergas project papers) lists, as line item 21, 'Construction of a reserve gas pipeline (looping) Du 1020mm, 130 km long, to the existing Makat-North Caucasus main gas pipeline', executor QazaqGaz, commissioning act year 2023, cost 89.1 billion tenge per the approved working design. (3) Independently, both astanatimes.com and inform.kz (Kazinform — one underlying news-wire story, so counted as one further corroborating but non-independent origin) report QazaqGaz and the Atyrau Region Akimat physically launching this 'looping (second line)' on 30 May 2023 in Makat district, cost ~86 billion tenge ($192.2M). All three describe the SAME physical, currently-operating asset. None of these sources are gem.wiki, GEM, abarrelfull, theodora, or wikidot — all fetched live and verified this session (gov.kz and adilet.zan.kz both required insecure-TLS retry per the documented cert-chain issue, not a liveness problem).

validity.researcher_notes: CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED. The gov.kz EIA document repeatedly and explicitly calls both the parent line and this loop a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) carrying natural gas ('природный газ'). It is a dedicated capacity-reserve/backup line paralleling an export trunk line for the first 130 km of its route, not a gathering, processing, or distribution line — transmission is the correct GGIT category. Not a duplicate commodity issue either: purely gas, no NGL/oil component described anywhere.

validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE CHECK vs P1476 (same pipeline name 'Makat–North Caucasus Pipeline', 944 km, cap 21.9, Makat->Chechnya, built 1986-1988) — the two rows share a name and gem.wiki page, so this is the obvious duplicate/relabel risk on the roster. RESOLVED, NOT a duplicate or a double-count: the gov.kz EIA document is explicit that P3999 is a NEW, physically distinct 'reserve pipeline (looping)' running PARALLEL to the 'existing' (существующего) single-strand ('однониточный, не имеет альтернативной нитки') main line only over its FIRST 130 of 944 km (Du1020mm loop vs the main line's Du1420mm), designed and built 2020-2023 — more than three decades after the 1986-1988 main line — for the stated purpose of avoiding supply outages during maintenance ('позволит избежать чрезвычайные ситуации, связанные с остановкой однонитоци [газопровода]'). The government's own Complex Plan (Resolution 488) lists this as a SEPARATE capital line item from any work on the main trunk. This is the same legitimate parallel-loop pattern already seen elsewhere on the Kazakhstan gas roster (e.g. P2289/P5695 Bukhara-Ural). No merge recommended.

validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION — Owner, LIKELY MISATTRIBUTED for this specific row. GEM currently has Owner1=Gazprom PJSC, Owner2=QazaqGaz for the LOOPING LINE (P3999) — the same owner pairing as the historic 1986-88 export trunk (P1476). But every source I found that discusses funding/ownership of the loop SPECIFICALLY (as opposed to the parent trunk in general) names only Kazakh state entities: (1) the Government's Complex Plan (Resolution 488, adilet.zan.kz) names 'QazaqGaz' as sole executor and states financing as '20% собственные средства Фонда [Samruk-Kazyna] и 80% собственные средства QazaqGaz' — no Gazprom financing share at all; (2) the gov.kz EIA document names AO 'Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya' as customer/заказчик; (3) intergas.kz's own 'About the Company' page (live-verified) states in plain English that Intergas Central Asia 'is a subsidiary of the National Company QazaqGaz, JSC' — no Gazprom equity mentioned anywhere in its corporate description. Gazprom's documented role on this SYSTEM is as operator of the connecting Russian-side pipeline (Mozdok-Kazimagomed, via 'Gazprom Transgaz Makhachkala') at the Kazakhstan-Russia interconnection point — a genuine fact about the wider export system, but not evidence of ownership of a 100%-Kazakh-funded, wholly-domestic 2020-2023 reserve/backup segment built to protect Atyrau region's OWN gas supply. (Note for context, not cited: gem.wiki's own infobox for this pipeline lists a SEPARATE owner field for the 'Looping/Second Line Segment' — 'QazaqGaz' only, no Gazprom — distinct from the main pipeline's 'Gazprom, Qazaqgaz'; i.e. even GEM's own source material distinguishes the two, and the sheet's Owner1=Gazprom for P3999 appears to not reflect that distinction.) I could not find an explicit ownership PERCENTAGE split for QazaqGaz/Intergas on this asset, so I'm not proposing exact numbers — recommend Update set Owner1=QazaqGaz (or Intergas Central Asia) and drop or demote Gazprom PJSC for this row.

summary: P3999 (Makat-North Caucasus Looping Line, 130km Du1020mm reserve loop) EXISTS and is correctly classified as an operating gas transmission line, confirmed at high tier by the Intergas EIA/working-design filing (gov.kz) and the Government's 2022 Complex Plan (adilet.zan.kz P2200000488), plus independent May-2023 launch coverage (astanatimes.com, inform.kz) — and it is NOT a duplicate of the parent P1476 trunk, which it parallels for only its first 130 of 944 km. Length=130km/Diameter=1020mm/Capacity=13.15bcm/y and Start=2023-05 all confirmed. Two real findings: (1) Owner1=Gazprom PJSC is very likely WRONG for this specific row — every source naming a funder/owner for the loop specifically says QazaqGaz/Intergas Central Asia, none say Gazprom — flagged as a concern with a recommended fix; (2) SegmentCost=86bn KZT matches the launch-day press figure but conflicts ~3.6% with the Government Complex Plan's 89.1bn 'actual PSD cost', logged not resolved. ProposalYear=2021 and ConstructionYear=2022 are UNRESOLVED — no live source pinned either year (an unverifiable, now-dead invest.gov.kz snippet suggested Nov 2021 construction start, not usable). EndLocation='Taldykol' is a soft, unconfirmed gap (sources name the endpoint 'CS Redut', not 'Taldykol', though they are likely the same place).
